title: Atezolizumab After Chemo-radiotherapy for muscle-invasive bladder cancer Patients Not Eligible for Radical Cystectomy
official: Bladder Sparing : Phase II study of maintenance anti-PD-L1 treatment with atezolizumab after chemo-radiotherapy for muscle-infiltrating bladder cancer patients not eligible for radical cystectomy
summary: Main objective: The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of maintenance therapy with atezolizumab, an anti-PD-L1, after chemo-radiotherapy for the treatment of patients with muscleinvasive bladder cancer not eligible for radical cystectomy, in terms of the disease-free survival (DFS) assessed at 2 years.

interventions.name: Tecentriq 1 200 mg concentrate for solution for infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Selection phase : Muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) pT2-T3 histologically confirmed
2. Selection phase : Haematological and biological parameters : White blood cell count ≥4000/mm3; Platelet count ≥100000 cells/mm3; Haemoglobin level ≥9 g/dL or corrected after transfusion; Adequate renal function: clearance >50 mL/min (Cockcroft); Adequate hepatic function: AST (SGOT) and ALT (SGPT) ≤2.5 x ULN, or ≤3.5 x ULN in the case of concurrent disease with known etiology and for which a corrective treatment is possible.
3. Selection phase : Patients of childbearing potential who agree to use a medically acceptable method of contraception during the study and for 120 days after the last study treatment. Women must have a negative urine or serum pregnancy test before receiving the study treatment and within 14 days prior to selection.
4. Selection phase : Patients having provided written informed consent prior to any study-related procedures.
5. Selection phase : Patients affiliated to the social security scheme.
6. Selection phase : Patients willing and able to comply with the scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures indicated in the protocol.
7. Inclusion phase : Patients who have received standard (chemo)-radiotherapy ≥60Gy or equivalent on the bladder according to the local practice.
8. Inclusion phase : The first administration of atezolizumab must be performed within 30 (+/-5) days after the last session of RT.
9. Inclusion phase : ECOG performance status ≤2.
10. Inclusion phase : Haematological and biological parameters : White blood cell count ≥3000/mm3; Platelet count ≥100000 cells/mm3; Haemoglobin level ≥9 g/dL or corrected after transfusion; Adequate renal function: clearance >50 mL/min (Cockcroft); Adequate hepatic function: AST (SGOT) and ALT (SGPT) ≤2.5 x ULN, or ≤3.5 x ULN in the case of concurrent disease with known etiology and for which a corrective treatment is possible; Adequate cardiac function: Troponin and CPK-MB at normal range.
11. Inclusion phase : Patients of childbearing potential who agree to use a medically acceptable method of contraception during the study and for 120 days after the last study treatment. Women must have a negative urine or serum pregnancy test before receiving the study treatment and within 14 days prior to inclusion.
12. Selection phase : Complete transurethral resection of bladder tumour (TURBT)
13. Inclusion phase : Patients having provided written informed consent prior to any study-related procedures.
14. Inclusion phase : Patients willing and able to comply with the scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures indicated in the protocol.
15. Selection phase : Patients for which chemo-radiotherapy is planned
16. Selection phase : No major pelvic involvement: pelvic nodes ≤15 mm on CT scan
17. Selection phase : No distant metastasis
18. Selection phase : Patient unfit for radical cystectomy because of age, comorbidities, or patient’s refusal
19. Selection phase : Patients ≥18 years old
20. Selection phase : ECOG performance status ≤2
21. Selection phase : Life expectancy ≥12 months
Exclusion criteria:
1. Selection phase : Patient with bladder carcinoma in situ (CIS).
2. Inclusion phase : In addition to the same non-inclusion criteria of selection phase that have to be respected, patients who have previously experienced a severe cutaneous reaction during previous treatment with an immune-stimulating anti-cancer agent.
3. Selection phase : Prior pelvic irradiation.
4. Selection phase : MIBC histology other than urothelial or squamous cell carcinomas (e.g., adenocarcinomas, micropapillary, sarcomas, or small cell histological types).
5. Selection phase : History of neoplastic disease, during the 3 years before selection, except completely resected cutaneous basal-cell carcinomas, carcinoma in-situ or localised prostate cancer without biochemical recurrence following definitive treatment.
6. Selection phase : Prior treatment with CD137 agonists or immune checkpoint inhibitors, including anti-cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen 4 (anti-CTLA-4), anti-programmed death-1 receptor (anti- PD-1), and anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (anti-PD-L1) therapeutic antibodies.
7. Selection phase : Contraindications for pelvic radiotherapy (e.g., inflammatory bowel disease).
8. Selection phase : History of immunodeficiency, including HIV infection, or systemic steroid therapy for any other disease.
9. Selection phase : A history of active autoimmune disease, except autoimmune-related hypothyroidism and type I diabetes mellitus
10. Selection phase : History of severe allergic anaphylactic reactions to chimeric, human or humanised antibodies, or fusion proteins.
11. Selection phase : Known hypersensitivity to Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell products or any component of the atezolizumab formulation.
12. Selection phase : Prior allogeneic stem cell or solid organ transplant.
13. Selection phase : Patients with the following severe acute co-morbidity are not eligible : Unstable angina or congestive heart failure that required hospitalisation in the 6 months before selection; Transmural myocardial infarction in the 6 months prior to selection; Acute bacterial or fungal infection requiring intravenous antibiotics at selection; Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation or other respiratory illness requiring hospitalisation or precluding study therapy at the time of selection; Severe hepatic disease: Child-Pugh Class B or C.
14. Selection phase : Patients with any other disease or illness which requires hospitalisation or is incompatible with the study treatment are not eligible.
15. Selection phase : Patients unable to comply with study obligations for geographic, social, or physical reasons, or who are unable to understand the purpose and procedures of the study.
16. Selection phase : Patients enrolled in another therapeutic study within 30 days of selection.
17. Selection phase : Pregnant or breast feeding women.
18. Selection phase : Person deprived of their liberty or under protective custody or guardianship.
